This role is for one of our clients 
 Compensation: $33.58 per hour 
 Fluent Language Skills Required:  Japanese. Native fluency in Japanese, including full command of kanji, hiragana and katakana, is required for this position. All annotation and transcription work is performed in Japanese.
 Why This Role Exists 
 Document understanding breaks down fastest in the languages that parsing and vision-language models rarely see. This project builds training data for exactly those languages: Japanese, alongside Korean and five Indic scripts. Each task takes a real, publicly available PDF page and produces a complete structural map of that page, paired with a faithful transcription of every text region in the original script.
 The dataset deliberately concentrates on the material models handle worst: handwriting, dense multi-column layouts, vertical text, tables, diagrams, and mixed-script pages. Documents are drawn from newspapers, textbooks, examinations, and everyday formats such as flyers, forms, manuals, menus, brochures, notices and worksheets, so that the corpus reflects the real diversity of Japanese documents rather than a narrow band of easily parsed ones.
 Delivered work is human-authored throughout. Component identification, component typing, reading order and all transcription are performed by people, not generated by parsing models.
 What You'll Do 
 Open and check a task: pages are provided, so you do not source documents yourself. We find the PDFs and upload them for you. Before annotating, confirm the page is in Japanese, is legible, has real content, and shows no personal details
 Annotate structure: identify and bound every meaningful region of the page - document title, section heading, paragraph, list, table, figure, diagram, caption, formula, question, answer field - and assign each a component type and a reading-order index
 Record relationships: link each region to the figure or table it belongs to through a parent component identifier
 Transcribe faithfully: reproduce all text exactly as it appears, including kanji, hiragana, katakana, furigana and handwritten content, flagging any region where the source is not legible
 Capture page metadata: language, document type, source, page dimensions, and flags for tables, formulas and handwriting
 Review a colleague's work: every task is reviewed end to end by a second Japanese expert, and experienced annotators take on that review
 Who You Are 
 You are a native Japanese speaker with full command of kanji, hiragana and katakana, including furigana and variant character forms
 You have professional experience in interpretation, journalism, transcription, translation, editorial work, or comparable document-intensive work
 You are exact: character-level accuracy matters more here than speed, and a single wrong character is a defect
 You are systematic: you apply a taxonomy consistently across hundreds of pages rather than improvising per document
 You are comfortable with unfamiliar layouts: vertical text, multi-column newspapers, exam papers, handwritten forms
 Nice-to-Have Specialties 
 AI training data: annotation, labeling, grading, or bilingual evaluation for training datasets
 Transcription and localization: MTPE, subtitling, bilingual QA, OCR correction or post-editing
 Document production: typesetting, copy-editing, proofreading, or digitization of Japanese-language material
 Script and encoding: Unicode normalization, Japanese input methods, full-width and half-width forms, and kanji variant handling
 What Success Looks Like 
 Every meaningful region on the page is captured, correctly bounded and correctly typed
 Reading order reflects how the page is actually read, including vertical text and multi-column layouts
 Transcriptions match the source character for character, in Japanese script rather than romaji
 Your tasks pass second-expert review the first time
 Unsuitable pages are flagged up front rather than after thirty minutes of work

Reporting to the VP, Financial Planning & Analysis, the Strategic Financial Analyst will be the financial architect for Trulioo’s biggest strategic bets, working side-by-side with the VP of FP&A. This isn't a reporting FP&A role, it’s a high-ownership position where you’ll build the models that actually drive our strategic growth, forecasting, and capital allocation. You’ll live in the data, breaking down unit economics and stress-testing assumptions until you find the hidden levers that move the needle.



We want an AI-native analyst that uses AI as a daily tool for automating repetitive tasks, and surfacing patterns in complex transaction data. You should comfortably integrate  Claude or similar tools to accelerate your workflow, prompt financial models, and analyze data outputs. You view AI as an essential asset that adds real leverage to financial analysis, driving better forecasts and reporting, faster iteration, and amplified analytical rigour.



This will be a full-time, permanent position working out of the Vancouver office on a hybrid model (3-days per week in the office).




WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:

Financial Planning, Performance & Reporting

 - Budgeting & AOP: Lead the annual operating planning process for your business segment, working across departments to build realistic, data-driven financial targets that align with company strategy.

 - Rolling Forecasting: Manage and refine rolling forecasts to provide leadership with dynamic, forward-looking insights that adapt to changing business conditions.

 - Performance Tracking & Variance Insights: Analyze monthly and quarterly results against prior periods and budgets, breaking down and escalating major variances with clear strategic context.

 - Executive & Board Communications: Collaborate with the VP of FP&A to craft clear, compelling financial narratives, KPI dashboards, quarterly board materials and investor updates.

Strategic Analysis & Growth Initiatives

 - Unit Economics & Margin Optimization: Deeply analyze margin drivers, such as transaction volumes, pricing structures, and product mix, to evaluate levers that impact EBITDA.

 - Cross-Functional Partnership: Serve as the strategic financial voice across the organization, partnering with leaders in Sales, Product, Operations, and Customer Success to model growth initiatives.

 - Strategic & M&A Modeling: Construct sophisticated multi-scenario financial models to guide corporate development, M&A diligence, integration, and strategic expansion initiatives.

Data, AI & Infrastructure

 - KPI Frameworks & Dashboards: Maintain accountability across the organization by defining key metrics for unit economics and efficiency, establishing automated dashboards to measure what matters.

 - Data Governance & Analytics: Ensure the absolute integrity of financial datasets by aggregating information from diverse sources and partnering across the organization to enhance transactional data flows.

 - AI Integration & Automation: Leverage advanced LLMs and AI tools to accelerate workflows, automate reporting pipelines, optimize forecasting models, and flag transaction anomalies.






WHAT YOU’LL BRING:

FP&A & Strategic Finance

 - 2–3 years of hands-on analyst or FP&A experience in fintech, payments, or transaction-focused industries.

 - Deep modeling expertise: Adept at modeling unit economics, transaction volumes, and pricing structures.

 - Metrics & Profitability mastery: Deep understanding of cohort profitability, CAC/LTV dynamics, and the precise bottom-line impact of minor pricing adjustments.


Corporate Development & M&A

 - 1–2 years of experience within corporate development, private equity, or junior investment banking.

 - Diligence & Leadership exposure: Firsthand experience building and defending robust financial models during due diligence and high-level leadership meetings.


Attention to Detail and Rigour

AI-Native Mindset

Intellectual Curiosity

Hi! I’m Steph , Head of Growth for Data Products at Modash.
 I joined Modash to help grow a newer and increasingly important side of our business:  our Data products. 
 Today, more than 100 companies using Modash data to power their own products and businesses. They’re building creator discovery tools, enriching their own datasets, powering workflows, and solving problems we probably haven't even thought of yet. And we're growing quickly.
 A huge part of that growth isn't just finding new customers. It's helping the customers we already have  build better products, get more value from our data, and grow with us .
 That's where you come in.
 Scope of the role & what you'll actually do
 We currently have two Technical CSMs in Canada and one in Europe, and we're hiring another  based in Toronto, Canada . Your job is simple to explain and hard to do well:  help customers turn Modash data into successful products, and own the outcome when getting there gets messy. 
 You'll own the entire journey for our API customers: from onboarding and adoption to expansion and long-term growth. Doing this well means becoming an extension of their team: understanding what they're building, where they're going, and how Modash can help them get there.
 1. Own your portfolio of accounts 
 You'll manage a portfolio of customers using one or both of our APIs. Success is measured mainly through Net Revenue Retention (NRR) and the work that drives it.
 You'll:
 Build clear success plans with goals, priorities and next steps
 Run regular customer calls and proactively keep things moving
 Understand what customers are building and help them use the right data and endpoints
 Troubleshoot technical issues and own getting them resolved
 Spot risks early and create a plan
 Find new ways Modash can help customers grow
 Own expansion end-to-end, from spotting the opportunity to closing the upgrade
 Own renewals and keep your accounts organised and up to date
 2. Onboard new customers 
 Once a customer buys Modash, you'll become one of their closest partners here.
 You'll:
 Run a strong Sales → CS handover
 Understand what they're building and what success looks like
 Create a clear integration plan with milestones and owners
 Help them make the right technical decisions and remove blockers
 Help them get to first value quickly
 Leave every interaction with clear next steps, owners and dates
 3. Collaborate across Modash 
 You'll be the voice of your customers internally.
 You'll work closely with Product to bring them clear customer problems and opportunities, connect customers for discovery and testing, coordinate with Sales on expansion, work with Support and Engineering on technical issues, and help Marketing turn what we're learning into useful customer resources.
 Even when other teams are involved,  you own driving the customer outcome forward. 
 The tools you'll use: 
 Vitally  → Customer Success CRM
 Notion  → internal knowledge
 Intercom  → customer communication and support
 Stripe  → subscriptions and invoices
 FullStory  → debugging and customer behaviour
 Calendly  → scheduling
 2+ years in Technical Customer Success, Account Management, Technical Account Management, or a similar customer-facing role
 Experience working with APIs or data products , or a background in a technical, product management or product owner role
 Comfortable discussing APIs, integrations and data flows. You don't need to code, but you should be technically curious to understand.
 You lead customers, rather than simply support them.  You ask good questions, understand the real problem and help decide what happens next
 You take ownership.  When something gets messy, you simplify it, make a judgement and drive it to an outcome
 You're a clear, concise communicator who can make complicated things simple
 You're commercially minded and naturally look for ways customers can get more value and grow their business
 You're proactive, organised and comfortable working without a perfect playbook
 Strong written and spoken English

 Experience with creator data or creator marketing
 Experience owning renewals and expansion
 Some coding or data experience, such as reading code, writing small scripts or SQL

 Compensation . CAD ca 150,000 to 170,000 on-target earnings (OTE) per year + stock options.

 Personal development.  We'll support courses, books or conferences that help you grow.
 Ownership.  Data is an important growth area for Modash. You'll have the autonomy to make decisions, try things and help shape how this part of the business grows.
 A little bit more about us...
 Founded in 2018 by a high-school dropout and a Canadian (yes, we’re also shocked it’s going so well), Modash is building a suite of tools that help brands scale partnerships with online content creators.
 2,700+ companies like Stanley 1913, Sennheiser, and NordVPN already use Modash to manage and scale their influencer marketing work. And we're just getting started. Over the coming decade, brand investment in creators will continue to boom, and Modash will be at the centre of it all.
 Modash is here to stay. We have 8-figures in ARR across two products, a $12M series A investment , and we are default alive. We are building a company that will still be here in 20 years; not rushing towards an exit.
 We’re almost 100 people distributed across 20+ countries, operating with a fast, async-first culture. If you join Modash, you’ll be surrounded by people who truly want to be the greatest at their craft. People who make you better. Interesting people too, who have done everything from building solar cars, to hanging out with Metallica and Bon Jovi.

 Student support resources available within the School of Pharmacy, the University, and the broader community.

 Academic progression requirements;  
 Program regulations and policies;  
 Professionalism expectations, learner conduct, and support for professional development  
 Academic standing and performance concerns;  
 Leaves of absence, program interruptions, and return-to-study planning;

 Financial aid, awards, bursaries, and referral to Student Awards and Financial Aid (SAFA) and other funding resources;   
 Career exploration and professional development opportunities.

 Monitors student academic performance and progression throughout the term through the use of reports, grade reviews, and other available data to identify students who may be experiencing academic difficulty; 
 Collaborates with the Undergraduate Program Manager to develop and implement appropriate interventions and escalation strategies. For students both on campus and on clinical placements, initiates proactive outreach and advising appointments with students who may be at academic risk and supports the development, implementation, and monitoring of remediation plans, including academic and professionalism remediation initiatives; liaises with Experiential staff to support students on placement

 Information sessions;  
 Applicant events;  
 Community outreach initiatives.

Job Description Summary 
We are looking for a senior OT cybersecurity engineer to join the Grid Automation Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (COE). The COE is a new central team within the Grid Automation OT Cybersecurity Product Line, and it owns how cybersecurity is delivered on Grid Automation projects worldwide.
This is a hands-on role. You will design, build, configure, test and, where needed, commission security solutions on complex utility and industrial projects. You will then turn that work into the standards, templates, scripts and training that regional teams use on every project that follows.
You will be the recognized technical owner for a set of solutions in the GA cybersecurity portfolio. Regional teams will come to you when a project goes beyond their experience.
Projects are grouped into three tiers, and the region manages the customer relationship on all of them. On complex (Tier 1) projects, the COE leads cybersecurity execution. On standard (Tier 2) projects, the region delivers using the COE toolkit, with COE support and training. On routine (Tier 3) projects, the region works independently and the COE reviews key milestones. 
You will also make delivery faster and more consistent by automating repeatable work in PowerShell and using frontier AI models to speed up documentation, requirements mapping and configuration reviews. 
 Job Description 
 Roles and Responsibilities
  Project Execution 
 Lead the cybersecurity workstream on Tier 1 projects end to end: requirements review, security architecture, detailed design, build, configuration, FAT, SAT, commissioning and handover.
 Produce the project security deliverables: security plan, zone and conduit model, risk assessment, hardening records, test procedures and reports, and the security handover package.
 Map customer requirements to contract scope early, flag deviations as they arise, and give project managers the technical basis for change orders.
  Execution Standards & Toolkit 
 Act as the technical owner (Expert) for an assigned set of COE competencies. Set the reference configuration for each and keep it current with product and partner releases.
 Build the GA execution toolkit as a by-product of delivery: reference architectures, configuration baselines, build checklists, PowerShell scripts, how-to guides, test procedures and templates.
 Automation 
 Write and maintain PowerShell scripts and modules that automate repeatable execution tasks.
 Build automated checks that compare as-built systems against the COE reference baselines and produce the evidence for milestone reviews, FAT and SAT.
 Use frontier AI models to speed up execution work.
 Competency building & Specialist Support 
 Design and deliver structured technical training for regional engineers, from foundation to advanced level, on the solutions you own.
 Track IEC 62443, NERC CIP, NIS2, CRA, IEC 62351 and regional mandates, and translate new requirements into execution checklists and deliverables.
 Required Qualifications
 Bachelor's or master's degree in Electrical, Electronics or Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or equivalent experience, with minumum 8 years in industrial automation or the energy sector, including at least 5 years of hands-on OT cybersecurity delivery on customer projects.
 Applied knowledge of IEC 62443 on real projects (especially parts 3-2, 3-3 and 2-4), working knowledge of NERC CIP, NIS2, CRA, IEC 62351 and NIST, and a sound understanding of substation and grid automation systems and protocols such as IEC 61850, DNP3, IEC 60870-5-104 and Modbus.
 Expert, hands-on skills in at least three of these areas, and working knowledge of most of the others: firewalls (Fortinet preferred), OT network monitoring (Nozomi, Dragos or similar), secure remote access (Xona or similar), Active Directory (Group Policy, RADIUS, LDAP), PKI, SIEM, Centralized security management platforms, application control (Trellix or similar), backup and recovery, Windows and Linux server build (hardening & virtualization), and hardening of field devices (IEDs, RTUs and gateways).
 Working proficiency in PowerShell for Windows Server and Active Directory administration. 
 Proven ability to produce security documentation that customers and auditors accept, experience training engineers and willingness to travel 20–40%, including extended site stays and ability to work across time zones.
 Desired Characteristics
 Certifications such as GICSP, GRID, ISA/IEC 62443 Cybersecurity Expert, CISSP, Fortinet FCP or FCSS (formerly NSE 4 and NSE 7) or Splunk Core Certified, or vendor training – Nozomi/Dragos.
 Experience as the cybersecurity lead on large utility, data center or industrial projects with multiple vendors and demanding customers.
 Experience building AI-assisted engineering workflows, such as prompt libraries, agent-based tools or API integrations, for documentation, requirements mapping, etc.
 Configuration-as-code and scripting experience: PowerShell DSC or Ansible, Python for Linux.
 Communicates clearly: writes procedures other engineers can follow without help, and explains and defends design decisions with both junior engineers and customer security teams.
 Holds scope boundaries with customers firmly and professionally, knowing this discipline protects both schedule and margin.
 Experience working in a global, multicultural organization. Additional languages are a plus.
 Takes ownership: when a problem appears on one project, fixes the toolkit so it does not happen again.

Our company builds technology that reshapes how people search, reason, and interact with the world around them. Week after week, we observe increasing demand for programmatic interfaces to that technology. The API Platform engineering team is charged with designing, implementing, and scaling these interfaces.

As a member of our team, you'll work on an eclectic portfolio spanning distributed systems, performance optimization, agent orchestration, and frontier topics that often change with each passing month. Throughout this work, you'll prioritize great developer and agent experience alike. You'll also define technical strategy for how we scale to meet compounding growth exponentials (number of customers, agents per customer, compute/retrieval per agent, etc.).




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, and operate mission-critical APIs that provide our customers the building blocks for frontier intelligence.

 - Own and evolve the API gateway and routing layer: authentication, authorization, rate limiting and quotas, usage metering, and request routing across heterogeneous upstream services.

 - Build API governance into the platform: contract-first schemas, breaking-change detection in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from a single source of truth.

 - Collaborate across teams to bring novel frontier capabilities into the API Platform, and partner with infrastructure teams on compute, networking, secrets, and security.

 - Continually reimagine the customer needs of tomorrow (and the architectures to serve those needs), while faithfully serving the customer workloads of today.

 - Uphold engineering excellence through design reviews, code quality, and internal documentation.




QUALIFICATIONS

 - Hands-on experience building and operating API gateways, reverse proxies, or routing layers: authentication and authorization, rate limiting and quotas, request routing, traffic shaping, and per-request observability.

 - Experience building API governance tooling: contract-first API design, breaking-change detection and API linting in CI, versioning and deprecation workflows, and SDKs and documentation generated from the contract.

 - Platform depth across the build and deploy path: you have owned CI/CD pipelines, container builds and base images, infrastructure as code, and progressive delivery (canary or blue-green) on a major cloud.

 - Strong customer empathy and product sense, ensuring the APIs you build are ergonomic, well-documented, and easy to adopt for developers and agents alike.

Strong plus:

 - Usage-based billing and metering systems, multi-tenant organization and identity models, and usage analytics pipelines.

 - Observability for API platforms: structured logging pipelines, metrics, tracing, and SLO tooling.

 About the Role 
 GE Vernova is executing its most significant engineering talent transformation in a generation. Engineer 2030 is GE Vernova's strategy to double engineering productivity while ensuring the company has the deep domain expertise and skills needed to scale the company while embracing the world's most consequential energy challenges.
 This is a program architect role for someone who can hold strategy and execution simultaneously to leverage the existing talent ecosystem to build engineering-specific solutions and drive adoption across businesses to build capabilities. This leader will be an early adopter and practitioner of AI-enabled workforce intelligence tools, applying emerging capabilities to improve the quality, speed, and precision of engineering capability decisions.
 The Senior Manager - - Engineering Capability & Transformation Leader is the engineer   behind the Talent & Skills workstream, one of five workstreams of Engineer 2030. This role is part of the Engineering & Technology Excellence function within GE Vernova EDGE, reporting to the Engineering Operations and Lean Leader. This leader will also own stakeholder alignment with the executive sponsors of the Workstream.  The Work You Will Lead 
 GE Vernova's engineering talent model was built for a prior era and does not help us scale to meet the moment. It is reactive and optimized for single-business execution. About Portless 
 Portless helps fast-growing direct-to-consumer brands ship orders from our fulfillment centers in China straight to their customers in North America, the UK and beyond. Brands no longer have to import and warehouse inventory in every market, which frees up cash and cuts costs. 
 We run the whole chain: fulfillment, freight, customs clearance and last-mile delivery, tied together by our own software and AI. Our merchants are mid-market brands in apparel, beauty, electronics and home goods. 
 We are venture-backed and on track to double revenue in 2026. Our team works across North America, China and beyond. 
 You will own Portless's books end to end: the monthly close across our entities in North America and Asia, merchant billing and collections, cash, and our first external audit. You will lead our accounting team, most of whom are based in China, and build the processes and controls that let us keep growing fast. 
 This is a hands-on role. You will be in the reconciliations yourself before you hand them off, and you will have real ownership from day one. 
 What you'll own 
 Month-end close. Own the close calendar across all entities, including consolidation, intercompany and FX, and get it done faster each month. 
 Billing and order-to-cash. Make sure every merchant is billed correctly and on time. That includes rate-card changes, credit notes and waivers with clear approvals, duties, VAT and tariffs billed back accurately, and cash applied across Stripe and our other payment channels. 
 AR and collections. Keep AR reconciled to the bank and payment processors, set our bad-debt reserve policy, and run collections with our billing team. 
 Cash. Own the daily cash position and a 13-week forecast tied to the bank, plus payment runs and approvals. 
 Audit and diligence. Select and lead our first external audit, prepare the books for investor and lender diligence, and own monthly lender reporting. 
 Tax and compliance. Coordinate outside advisors on Canadian, US and Chinese filings, sales tax and VAT, and transfer pricing. 
 Systems and controls. Tighten our stack (QuickBooks Online, Stripe, Bill.com, Ramp), document how things get done, and decide when we need an ERP. 
 Team. Lead and develop the accounting team, give every process a clear owner, and work closely with our data and engineering teams on billing data. 
 What success looks like in your first year 
 Outcome 
 By 
 90 days 
 You own the daily cash position and monthly lender reporting, and the whole team works from one close calendar. 
 6 months 
 Every entity closes by business day 10, and every rate-card change, credit note and waiver has an approval trail. 
 12 months 
 Our first external audit is complete. AR ties to the bank and payment processors every month, and duties and VAT billed match what we paid. The team runs on documented processes. 
 What you bring 
 CPA, CA or an equivalent designation. 
 8+ years in accounting, including at least 3 as a controller or assistant controller who owned the close. 
 A start in audit at a Big 4 or mid-tier public accounting firm. 
 You have owned a multi-entity, multi-currency close, including consolidation and intercompany. 
 You have run billing and collections at a high-volume business that bills per order, per transaction or on usage. 
 You have taken a company through a first audit or an audit-readiness cleanup, working directly with the auditors. 
 You have led a team, including people in another country.
 You are comfortable with a lean stack and AI tools, and you keep your work auditable. Clear, direct written English. 
 Nice to have 
 Mandarin. Most of our accounting team is in China, so this is a big plus. 
 Experience in logistics, 3PL, freight forwarding, customs brokerage or cross-border e- commerce. 
 Accounting for duties, VAT and tariffs paid on behalf of customers, and for transfer pricing. 
 Financial due diligence or transaction services experience. An ERP implementation or migration, such as NetSuite. 
 How you work 
 You can't let a number go until it ties. 
 You stay calm and factual when things move fast. 
 You hold the line on controls, even when someone senior is asking for an exception. 
 You fix the biggest problems first instead of redesigning everything at once. 
 You are hands-on and low ego, and you'll do the reconciliations yourself until the team can. 
 You raise bad news early and say "I don't know" when you don't. 
 You manage across time zones and cultures with patience and clear writing.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.
 The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.
 * Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab. 
 About the role 
 We are looking for a Principal Engineer to help build GitLab Duo Agent Platform, the agentic orchestration layer that runs AI agents and flows across the entire software lifecycle.
 Principal Engineers at GitLab are recognized experts across multiple technology domains and represent the senior technical leadership within their organization. In this role you will set technical direction for a significant part of the Agent Platform, working across several teams to turn agentic capabilities into something engineering organizations can actually depend on: predictable, observable, governable, and fast enough to sit in the critical path of real development work.
 The Agent Platform is not a single service. It spans agent execution and orchestration, flow definition and event-driven triggering, the AI Catalog through which customers discover and manage agents, model routing and evaluation, and the governance surface that decides which agents may act where and under whose identity. It runs on GitLab.com, GitLab Dedicated, and Self-Managed installations, including deployments that use self-hosted models to meet compliance requirements. You will work on the parts of that system where the hard architectural questions live, and you will do it hands-on.
 This role reports into the VP of the AI Engineering organization and works closely with Engineering Managers, Staff Engineers, Product Management, Infrastructure and Security.
 What you'll do 
 Define the technical direction for a significant area of Duo Agent Platform across several teams, and partner with Engineering Managers and Product to turn it into a roadmap with a six-month horizon.
 Build the orchestration layer that makes agents and flows reliable: session lifecycle, tool invocation, context assembly, concurrency, retries, timeouts, and failure modes that degrade gracefully instead of stalling a developer's workflow.
 Hands on work on driving topics throughout the whole organisation from POC level, architecture to full implementation. 
 Participate in Incident Management on-call rotation, to help meet availability goals for GitLab.com.
 Strong product builder and ownership mentality. Understanding of product strategy, technical strategy, delivering customer value and iteration towards a successful product
 Write clear, opinionated design documents, architecture narratives, and decision records that let other teams make aligned decisions. Ensure the architecture holds across multi-tenant GitLab.com, Dedicated, and Self-Managed deployments, including self-hosted model configurations, and respects data governance boundaries in each.
 Use the platform on our own work, find where it falls short of what we claim, and feed that back through improvements into the product.
 Mentor Staff and Senior Engineers, and raise the bar for experimentation rigor and cross-team collaboration.
 Work across the whole platform on different projects, features and teams. This reaches across:
 Design the extensibility surface so customers can build custom agents and flows, connect their own tools and internal systems, and bring external agents such as Claude Code and Codex into GitLab workflows without weakening the platform's guarantees.
 Drive down the cost and latency of agentic requests, and work with Product on how model selection, routing, and credit consumption behave as usage grows.
 Define the evaluation practice for the platform: offline benchmarks and online experiments that measure task completion, correctness, tool-call accuracy, latency, and cost per task, and that catch regressions before customers do.
 Build the governance and safety surface with Security and Compliance: policy-driven controls over which agents and models may run where, permission and identity semantics that align to existing roles and group structure, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, traceability of every flow session, and audit that stands up to enterprise review.
 Complete Interview Training and participate in hiring for the department as a technical interviewer or panel member.
 What you'll bring 
 8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years at Staff, Principal level or equivalent senior technical leadership.
 Hands-on production experience building on large language models: agent loops, tool calling, context management, retrieval, prompt and model evaluation. Experience shipping this to real users, not only prototyping it.
 Strong background in distributed systems, including service decomposition, fault tolerance, observability, and operational resilience under multi-tenant load.
 A track record of defining evaluation frameworks and using benchmark and experiment results to make architecture decisions, rather than shipping on intuition.
 Experience designing human-in-the-loop controls, safety guardrails, and responsible AI practices for systems that act on a customer's behalf.
 Ability to drive alignment across Engineering, Product, Infrastructure, and Security on problems that start out ambiguous.
 Experience mentoring senior engineers and shaping technical direction across multiple teams without direct authority.
 Comfort working in one or more of Ruby, Go, Python, or TypeScript, and willingness to work across the stack the platform spans.
 Excellent written and asynchronous communication, and the ability to work effectively in a fully remote, globally distributed organization.
 About the team 
 The AI engineering organisation is building the product and infrastructure that make GitLab an effective environment for running agents across the software development lifecycle. We’re distributed across the world and partner with teams throughout GitLab to help the GitLab Duo Agent Platform become the backbone of GitLab's AI features. You will report directly to the VP of Engineering for AI and especially work together with all the teams, the engineering management and other principal engineers in the AI department. This is an opportunity to lead a consequential group as AI changes how software is built.

No mandate to cut, flip, or roll up into something unrecognizable.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

Fresh off a $225M Series C, we're acquiring companies at pace and the hiring demand that comes with it is real. As we scale, we are looking to build our in-house business and G&A recruiting function, while also expanding our talent offerings to our portcos. This is a unique, multi-faceted role for a superstar generalist recruiter who can run full-cycle searches across finance, sales, marketing, operations, HR, and customer success, both at Beacon's corporate team and inside our portfolio companies.

 - Full-cycle ownership, corporate side. Support hiring for non-eng/non-product roles at Beacon HQ, including finance, marketing, sales, ops, M&A, and BD, from first outreach to signed offer.

 - Constant context-switching. Juggle multiple open roles at once across different functions, companies, and markets, each with its own comp band, hiring bar, and stakeholder.
